**RESPONSE_TO: ChatGPT (Round 4)**
I accept your challenge on `seal_epoch()` idempotency. Given Bug #40's deep-copy fix on `.records`/`.epochs`, and no in-module mutator besides `append_record`/`seal_epoch`/`load_json`, the only reachable path to duplicate sealing is crash-between-seal-and-save, which the idempotency guard handles correctly. I am not re-filing it. I am filing a related but distinct concern: `seal_epoch()` seals over unverified records when called via the API (not CLI). See CC2_F005.

**RESPONSE_TO: Gemini (Round 4)**

@ChatGPT: Your ChatGPT_F001 (deep-copy rebinding fix) is strong and I confirm the mechanism. One gap: your proposed rebinding code builds `current_by_id` from `new_findings + barrier_rejected`, but `barrier_rejected` contains the ORIGINAL `new_findings` objects (before DC/NK processing), not the triaged copies. The `finding_id` keys will match, but `barrier_rejected` findings were never in `filtered` or `rejected` — they were pre-filtered. The rebinding should be against `new_findings` only: `current_by_id = {f.finding_id: f for f in new_findings}`.

@Gemini: Your Gemini_F001 LOCK fix is architecturally correct but CC2_F001 above extends it: DUPLICATE verdicts (especially from the bug-closed gate) must also be locked. Without this, autoimmune override resurrects findings about already-closed bugs — exactly the scenario the NK bug-closed gate was designed to prevent.

@DeepSeek: Your DeepSeek_F003 (PENDING) about `regulatory_t_v2_shadow` missing the UNCERTAIN rate check — confirmed still present in the artifact. Since v2 is PRIMARY, this is a live gap. The v1 UNCERTAIN check (Check 1b) is dead code in practice because `autoimmune_flag = v2_autoimmune`.

Definitive stance: Six findings filed. CC2_F001 (LOCK gap for DUPLICATE verdicts under autoimmune override) and CC2_F002 (response truncation corrupting post-recovery relay) are the highest-impact. CC2_F003-F004 address manifest inflation and partial-grounding misattribution in the B-Cell v2 prover. CC2_F005-F006 are defense-in-depth and formatting consistency respectively.
